subject: Arabic
source: Drive: Curriculum/Arabic folder and Schemes of work/Arabic (GCSE-Arabic-2017 Scheme of Work, Pearson, for progression); TGA Year 7 Arabic file for continuity (greetings, family, possession, hobbies); Madinah-style progression of present and past tense verbs

lessons.unit: Unit 1: My home and where things are
lessons.title: My house and its rooms
objectives: Name the main rooms and parts of a house in Arabic
Use هَذَا and هَذِهِ correctly with masculine and feminine nouns
Say what you do in each room using present tense verbs
starter: Say in Arabic: 'This is my father's book' using the possessive construct.
Say in Arabic: 'I have a brother and a sister'.
Greet a classmate and ask how they are, with the correct -ka or -ki ending.

teach.heading: Bismillah: the rooms of a house
bullets: بَيْتٌ - baytun - a house
غُرْفَةُ النَّوْمِ - ghurfatu n-nawm - bedroom
غُرْفَةُ الْجُلُوسِ - ghurfatu l-julūs - living room
مَطْبَخٌ - maṭbakhun - kitchen
حَمَّامٌ - ḥammāmun - bathroom
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Qur'an 16:80 says that Allah made your homes a place of rest (sakan), so start by thanking Allah for our homes. Show each word with a picture and have pupils repeat chorally, then individually. Point out the possessive construct: ghurfatu has no 'al' and no tanween because it is the first word of the construct; only the second word has 'al'. Ask pupils to find the words they already know from Year 7 (bayt).

teach.heading: More parts of the home
bullets: حَدِيقَةٌ - ḥadīqatun - garden
بَابٌ - bābun - door
نَافِذَةٌ - nāfidhatun - window
سَطْحٌ - saṭḥun - roof
سُلَّمٌ - sullamun - stairs, ladder
teach.note: Quick-fire game: say the English, pupils type or hold up the Arabic on a mini whiteboard. Note that most words ending in the tied taa marbuta (ة) are feminine: ḥadīqa, nāfidha. Check pronunciation of ح in ḥadīqa and ḥammām: it is breathy from the throat, not like English h.

teach.heading: This is...: هَذَا and هَذِهِ
bullets: هَذَا مَطْبَخٌ - hādhā maṭbakhun - this is a kitchen
هَذِهِ غُرْفَةٌ - hādhihi ghurfatun - this is a room
هَذِهِ حَدِيقَةٌ جَمِيلَةٌ - hādhihi ḥadīqatun jamīlatun - a beautiful garden
Masculine noun: هَذَا. Feminine noun: هَذِهِ
teach.note: Explain that Arabic has no word for 'is' here: the two nouns just sit side by side. Ask: how do we know whether to say hādhā or hādhihi? Rule of thumb: ة at the end means feminine. Misconception: pupils may think حَمَّامٌ is feminine because it sounds like a long word; it is masculine. Stretch: some feminine words have no ة, for example دَارٌ (house) and شَمْسٌ (sun).

teach.heading: What I do in each room
bullets: أَنَامُ فِي غُرْفَةِ النَّوْمِ - anāmu fī ghurfati n-nawm - I sleep
آكُلُ فِي الْمَطْبَخِ - ākulu fī l-maṭbakh - I eat
أَتَوَضَّأُ فِي الْحَمَّامِ - atawaḍḍa'u fī l-ḥammām - I make wudu
أَلْعَبُ فِي الْحَدِيقَةِ - alʿabu fī l-ḥadīqa - I play
teach.note: Recap the first-person present tense verbs from Year 6 (the أَ prefix). Point out that after فِي the noun ends with a kasra (-i): غُرْفَةِ, الْمَطْبَخِ, الْحَدِيقَةِ. Do not give a full grammar lecture: pupils just notice the pattern 'fī + the noun with -i'. Ask: where else could you make wudu? (at the sink in the bathroom).

teach.heading: Adab on entering the home
bullets: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ - as-salāmu ʿalaykum - peace be upon you
Say salaam when you enter your home
Greet your family with a smile
teach.note: Qur'an 24:61 tells us that when we enter houses we should greet one another with a greeting from Allah, blessed and good. Link to home adab: salaam to parents and siblings, remove shoes, keep the home tidy. Pupils write one sentence in Arabic about their favourite room, using هَذِهِ or هَذَا, and read it to a partner.

practice: Point to a picture and ask: هَذَا أَمْ هَذِهِ؟ (hādhā am hādhihi?) for مَطْبَخ, غُرْفَة, حَدِيقَة, حَمَّام, بَاب.
Complete: ___ حَمَّامٌ and ___ نَافِذَةٌ.
Translate: 'I eat in the kitchen' and 'I sleep in the bedroom'.
Say what you do in the garden using a verb from the lesson.
independent: Label a drawing of a house with at least eight Arabic words, each with a تَشْكِيل (vowel marks).
Write five sentences beginning هَذَا or هَذِهِ about your home.
Write four sentences saying what you do in different rooms, for example أَقْرَأُ فِي غُرْفَةِ الْجُلُوسِ.
exit: Write the Arabic for 'bedroom' and 'kitchen'.
Choose the correct word and say why: ___ بَابٌ (هَذَا / هَذِهِ).
lessons.homework: Draw your home and write ten Arabic labels and two sentences about what you do in two rooms.
lessons.send: SEND: picture word-bank with transliteration and a sentence frame (هَذِهِ ___). EAL: bilingual list with audio recording by the teacher. Stretch: add the feminine nouns without ة (دَارٌ, شَمْسٌ) and explain why they take هَذِهِ.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: My home and where things are
lessons.title: Where is it? Prepositions of place
objectives: Use prepositions of place to say where things are
Ask and answer questions with أَيْنَ
Use the correct genitive ending after a preposition
starter: Name five rooms of the house in Arabic.
Say 'This is a kitchen' and 'This is a garden' in Arabic.
Say what you do in the bedroom and in the garden.

teach.heading: Where is it? أَيْنَ؟
bullets: أَيْنَ الْمِفْتَاحُ؟ - ayna l-miftāḥ? - where is the key?
الْمِفْتَاحُ فِي الْحَقِيبَةِ - in the bag
أَيْنَ أَبِي؟ - ayna abī? - where is my father?
أَبِي فِي الْمَسْجِدِ - abī fī l-masjid - at the mosque
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Ask a question with أَيْنَ and have pupils answer with a sentence. Point out the pattern: question word + noun, answer: noun + فِي + noun with kasra. Pupils can look around their own room via camera and ask each other where an object is.

teach.heading: On, under, above
bullets: الْكِتَابُ عَلَى الْمَكْتَبِ - al-kitābu ʿalā l-maktab - on the desk
الْقِطَّةُ تَحْتَ الطَّاوِلَةِ - al-qiṭṭatu taḥta ṭ-ṭāwila - under the table
الْمِصْبَاحُ فَوْقَ السَّرِيرِ - al-miṣbāḥu fawqa s-sarīr - above the bed
teach.note: Use real objects on screen and move them to demonstrate. Notice the noun after each preposition ends in a kasra: الْمَكْتَبِ, الطَّاوِلَةِ, السَّرِيرِ. Misconception: pupils keep the damma (nominative) ending on the second noun. Drill: say a preposition and a noun, pupils add the right ending.

teach.heading: In front of, behind, between
bullets: الْحَدِيقَةُ خَلْفَ الْبَيْتِ - al-ḥadīqatu khalfa l-bayt - behind the house
السَّيَّارَةُ أَمَامَ الْبَابِ - as-sayyāratu amāma l-bāb - in front of the door
الْمَسْجِدُ بِجَانِبِ الْمَدْرَسَةِ - next to the school
teach.note: Note that أَمَامَ and خَلْفَ and فَوْقَ and تَحْتَ and بَيْنَ end with a fatha because they are words for position, but the noun after them still takes kasra. Practise: بَيْنَ الْمَطْبَخِ وَغُرْفَةِ الْجُلُوسِ (between the kitchen and the living room). Pupils draw a simple floor plan from the teacher's spoken description.

teach.heading: Describe a room
bullets: فِي غُرْفَتِي سَرِيرٌ - fī ghurfatī sarīrun - in my room is a bed
السَّرِيرُ بِجَانِبِ النَّافِذَةِ - next to the window
الْمَكْتَبُ أَمَامَ الْبَابِ - the desk is in front of the door
الْمِصْبَاحُ عَلَى الْمَكْتَبِ - the lamp is on the desk
teach.note: Show how to build a short description: where + what + where it is. Note the word order: the place comes first, then the thing in it (فِي غُرْفَتِي سَرِيرٌ). Pupils describe their room orally in pairs using at least four prepositions. Praise accurate vowel endings.

teach.heading: Cleanliness and tidy homes
bullets: الطُّهُورُ شَطْرُ الْإِيمَانِ - aṭ-ṭuhūru shaṭru l-īmān - purity is half of faith
غُرْفَتِي مُرَتَّبَةٌ - ghurfatī murattabatun - my room is tidy
غُرْفَتِي نَظِيفَةٌ - ghurfatī naẓīfatun - my room is clean
teach.note: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said that purity is half of faith (Sahih Muslim). Link tidy, clean rooms to ihsan, doing things well. Practise the sentences غُرْفَتِي مُرَتَّبَةٌ and غُرْفَتِي نَظِيفَةٌ with different adjectives. Note that غُرْفَتِي is feminine, so the adjective ends in ة. Ask pupils to give one thing they do to keep their room clean.

practice: Say where the book is: on the desk, under the bed, behind the door.
Add the correct ending: الْقِطَّةُ فِي الْحَدِيقَ___ (a/ah/ati).
Ask 'Where is my pen?' and answer 'It is on the table'.
Describe the picture the teacher shares using three prepositions.
independent: Draw a room and write six sentences saying where six objects are.
Read the sentences to a partner who draws what they hear, then check.
Write two questions with أَيْنَ and their answers.
exit: Write: 'The book is under the table' in Arabic.
What vowel ending does the noun take after فِي?
lessons.homework: Write a description of your bedroom with at least six prepositions of place.
lessons.send: SEND: preposition cards with pictures and colour-coded kasra endings. EAL: matching task for English and Arabic prepositions. Stretch: add مُقَابِلَ (opposite) and حَوْلَ (around) in sentences.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: My home and where things are
lessons.title: Adjectives: agreement with the noun
objectives: Place adjectives after the noun
Match the adjective to the noun in gender and definiteness
Tell the difference between a phrase and a sentence
starter: Say where the book is: on the desk, under the chair.
Which word do you use for 'this' with a feminine noun?
Translate: 'The garden is behind the house'.

teach.heading: Adjectives follow the noun
bullets: بَيْتٌ كَبِيرٌ - baytun kabīrun - a big house
غُرْفَةٌ صَغِيرَةٌ - ghurfatun ṣaghīratun - a small room
حَدِيقَةٌ جَمِيلَةٌ - ḥadīqatun jamīlatun - a beautiful garden
In Arabic the adjective comes after the noun
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Compare English 'a big house' with Arabic 'a house big'. Have pupils say the phrase in English word order and then flip it. Highlight that masculine adjectives have no ة and feminine ones add ة. Check that pupils repeat the vowel endings -un/-atun.

teach.heading: Match gender
bullets: مَطْبَخٌ جَدِيدٌ - maṭbakhun jadīdun - a new kitchen
نَافِذَةٌ جَدِيدَةٌ - nāfidhatun jadīdatun - a new window
غُرْفَةٌ وَاسِعَةٌ - ghurfatun wāsiʿatun - a spacious room
بَابٌ قَدِيمٌ - bābun qadīmun - an old door
teach.note: Sort a list of nouns into masculine and feminine, then add the right adjective. Misconception: pupils add ة to the noun and forget to add it to the adjective. Quick test: show a noun in Arabic and pupils say the matching adjective form.

teach.heading: Match definiteness: phrase or sentence?
bullets: الْبَيْتُ الْكَبِيرُ - al-baytu l-kabīru - the big house
الْبَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ - al-baytu kabīrun - the house is big
الْغُرْفَةُ الْجَمِيلَةُ - al-ghurfatu l-jamīlatu - the beautiful room
الْغُرْفَةُ جَمِيلَةٌ - the room is beautiful
teach.note: The key point: if both words have 'al' the phrase is 'the big house' (a noun phrase); if only the noun has 'al', the adjective is the predicate and we get a full sentence 'the house is big'. Write both on the board and ask pupils which is a phrase and which is a sentence. Common error: الْبَيْتُ الْكَبِيرٌ (mixing al with tanween).

teach.heading: Plural things
bullets: بُيُوتٌ كَبِيرَةٌ - buyūtun kabīratun - big houses
غُرَفٌ جَمِيلَةٌ - ghurafun jamīlatun - beautiful rooms
Things (not people) in the plural take a feminine singular adjective
teach.note: This is an enrichment slide for stronger pupils. For plural nouns that are not people (houses, rooms, books) Arabic uses the feminine singular adjective. Do not expect everyone to apply this independently yet; praise those who notice it.

teach.heading: Using adjectives well
bullets: Use adjectives to add detail
غُرْفَتِي صَغِيرَةٌ وَجَمِيلَةٌ - small and beautiful
Join two adjectives with وَ
teach.note: Show how a sentence improves: غُرْفَةٌ becomes غُرْفَةٌ صَغِيرَةٌ وَنَظِيفَةٌ. Remind pupils that saying alhamdulillah for what we have is part of gratitude (shukr). Pupils write two sentences about their room in pairs and swap for peer checking of gender agreement.

practice: Add the correct adjective: بَيْتٌ (big), غُرْفَةٌ (small), مَطْبَخٌ (new).
Is it a phrase or a sentence? الْبَابُ الْقَدِيمُ / الْبَابُ قَدِيمٌ.
Translate: 'a spacious garden' and 'the new window'.
Correct the mistake: غُرْفَةٌ كَبِيرٌ.
independent: Write six noun phrases with a noun and a matching adjective.
Write four full sentences describing your house.
Turn two of your phrases into definite phrases with 'al' on both words.
exit: Write 'a big kitchen' and 'a big room' in Arabic.
What is the difference between الْبَيْتُ الْجَدِيدُ and الْبَيْتُ جَدِيدٌ?
lessons.homework: Write five sentences describing five things in your home using adjectives that agree with the noun.
lessons.send: SEND: colour code masculine (blue) and feminine (pink) cards. EAL: sentence builders with English glosses. Stretch: include non-human plural agreement (بُيُوتٌ كَبِيرَةٌ).

lessons.unit: Unit 1: My home and where things are
lessons.title: Describing my home in writing
objectives: Use هُنَاكَ and فِي بَيْتِي to say what there is
Write a paragraph of six to eight sentences about your home
Use possessive endings -ī and -nā
starter: Make a phrase: 'a small kitchen' and 'a new door'.
Where is the key? It is on the table. Say it in Arabic.
Name three rooms and say what you do in each.

teach.heading: My and our
bullets: بَيْتِي - baytī - my house
غُرْفَتِي - ghurfatī - my room
بَيْتُنَا - baytunā - our house
حَدِيقَتُنَا - ḥadīqatunā - our garden
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Revise the possessive endings: -ī (my), -nā (our). Note that the tied ة becomes an open ت before the ending: غُرْفَة → غُرْفَتِي. Misconception: writing غُرْفَةِي. Pupils transform five words from the board.

teach.heading: There is... هُنَاكَ
bullets: هُنَاكَ حَدِيقَةٌ - hunāka ḥadīqatun - there is a garden
هُنَاكَ مَطْبَخٌ كَبِيرٌ - there is a big kitchen
فِي بَيْتِي ثَلَاثُ غُرَفٍ - fī baytī thalāthu ghurafin - three rooms
فِي بَيْتِي غُرْفَتَانِ - fī baytī ghurfatāni - two rooms
teach.note: Explain that هُنَاكَ is invariable and the thing that exists follows it. Teach the two chunks 'ثَلَاثُ غُرَفٍ' and 'غُرْفَتَانِ' as ready-made phrases; do not teach the full number rules yet (stretch: the number ثَلَاثَة loses ة with a feminine noun). Pupils say how many rooms their home has.

teach.heading: Link ideas
bullets: وَ - wa - and
لَكِنَّ - lākinna - but
أَيْضًا - aydan - also
لِأَنَّ - li-anna - because
teach.note: Show a bare sentence and then improve it with connectives. Example: بَيْتِي صَغِيرٌ لَكِنَّهُ جَمِيلٌ (my house is small but it is beautiful). Note that لَكِنَّ takes a pronoun ending (-hu). Provide an English-Arabic connectives card.

teach.heading: A model paragraph
bullets: بَيْتِي كَبِيرٌ وَجَمِيلٌ - baytī kabīrun wa-jamīlun
فِي بَيْتِي أَرْبَعُ غُرَفٍ - four rooms
هُنَاكَ حَدِيقَةٌ خَلْفَ الْبَيْتِ - a garden behind the house
أُحِبُّ بَيْتِي - uḥibbu baytī - I love my house
teach.note: Read the model together, then ask: what makes it good? Which adjectives, prepositions and connectives are used? Pupils annotate with colours. Remind them to check ة becoming ت before the possessive ending and to add vowel marks.

teach.heading: Writing check
bullets: Check gender agreement
Check the kasra after prepositions
Add vowels and a final الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ
teach.note: Introduce a self-check list on screen. Praise accurate vowelling. End the written task with الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ as a sign of gratitude. Pupils will write the full paragraph independently in the next section.

practice: Add 'my' to the words: غُرْفَة, حَدِيقَة, مَطْبَخ.
Say: 'There is a big garden in our house'.
Join two sentences with لَكِنَّ: بَيْتِي صَغِيرٌ / حَدِيقَتُنَا كَبِيرَةٌ.
independent: Write a paragraph of six to eight sentences about your home.
Use at least one هُنَاكَ, two prepositions of place, two adjectives and one connective.
Swap with a partner and use the checklist to correct two mistakes each.
exit: Write the Arabic for 'my room' and 'our garden'.
Complete: ___ حَدِيقَةٌ جَمِيلَةٌ (there is).
lessons.homework: Rewrite your paragraph neatly with full vowels and learn to read it aloud.
lessons.send: SEND: sentence starters and a word bank with images. EAL: model paragraph with audio. Stretch: add a comparison to a relative's home using مِثْلَ (like).

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Time and my daily routine
lessons.title: Telling the time
objectives: Ask and answer the time in Arabic
Say whole hours, half hours and quarter hours
Link times to the five daily prayers
starter: Say your address and name in Arabic.
Count from 11 to 20 in Arabic.
Name three days of the week you know.

teach.heading: Hours
bullets: كَمِ السَّاعَةُ؟ - kami s-sāʿa? - what time is it?
السَّاعَةُ الْوَاحِدَةُ - one o'clock
السَّاعَةُ الثَّانِيَةُ - two o'clock
السَّاعَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ - three o'clock
السَّاعَةُ الرَّابِعَةُ - four o'clock
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Qur'an 4:103 says prayer is prescribed for the believers at fixed times, so time matters in Islam. The hours use ordinal numbers that agree with السَّاعَةُ (feminine): الْخَامِسَةُ, السَّادِسَةُ, السَّابِعَةُ, الثَّامِنَةُ, التَّاسِعَةُ, الْعَاشِرَةُ. Drill by showing analogue clocks. Misconception: using the cardinal numbers (wāḥid, ithnān) rather than the ordinals.

teach.heading: Half and quarter
bullets: السَّاعَةُ الْخَامِسَةُ وَالنِّصْفُ - five thirty
السَّاعَةُ السَّابِعَةُ وَالرُّبْعُ - quarter past seven
السَّاعَةُ التَّاسِعَةُ إِلَّا رُبْعًا - quarter to nine
السَّاعَةُ الثَّانِيَةَ عَشْرَةَ - twelve o'clock
teach.note: Show the structure: السَّاعَةُ + hour + وَ + fraction, or hour + إِلَّا for 'to'. Note that 11 and 12 are الْحَادِيَةَ عَشْرَةَ and الثَّانِيَةَ عَشْرَةَ. Practise with a moving clock on screen. Pupils say the time and the next pupil says the time 15 minutes later.

teach.heading: Minutes
bullets: وَخَمْسُ دَقَائِقَ - wa-khamsu daqā'iq - and five minutes
وَعَشْرُ دَقَائِقَ - wa-ʿashru daqā'iq - and ten minutes
السَّاعَةُ الثَّامِنَةُ وَخَمْسُ دَقَائِقَ - 8:05
teach.note: Teach 5 and 10 minutes as chunks; the full number system for 'to' and 'past' is not needed yet. Check that pupils pronounce the ق of دَقَائِقَ deep in the throat. Do a quick time-telling quiz with five clock faces.

teach.heading: Prayer times
bullets: صَلَاةُ الْفَجْرِ - ṣalātu l-fajr - dawn prayer
صَلَاةُ الظُّهْرِ - ṣalātu ẓ-ẓuhr - noon prayer
صَلَاةُ الْعَصْرِ - ṣalātu l-ʿaṣr - afternoon prayer
صَلَاةُ الْمَغْرِبِ - ṣalātu l-maghrib - sunset prayer
صَلَاةُ الْعِشَاءِ - ṣalātu l-ʿishā' - night prayer
teach.note: Name the five prayers and ask pupils to put them in order. Example sentence: نُصَلِّي الظُّهْرَ فِي السَّاعَةِ الْوَاحِدَةِ (we pray Dhuhr at one o'clock). Times change through the year, so give an example from today's timetable. Ask: when does the school day pause for prayer?

teach.heading: Asking and answering
bullets: مَتَى صَلَاةُ الْعَصْرِ؟ - matā ṣalātu l-ʿaṣr? - when is Asr?
فِي السَّاعَةِ الثَّالِثَةِ - at three o'clock
مَتَى الدَّرْسُ؟ - matā d-dars? - when is the lesson?
teach.note: Use فِي السَّاعَةِ + ordinal with a kasra for 'at'. Pupils ask a partner when three events happen and record the answers. Check the new vowel ending on the ordinal after فِي: الثَّالِثَةِ.

practice: Write the time in numbers: السَّاعَةُ الثَّامِنَةُ وَالنِّصْفُ.
Ask a partner: 'When is the Maghrib prayer?'
Answer: 'The lesson is at nine o'clock'.
independent: Draw six clock faces and write the Arabic time under each.
Write a timetable of the five daily prayers with example times.
Role-play a conversation: asking the time and the time of a lesson.
exit: Write the Arabic for 'half past two'.
How do you say 'quarter to eight' in Arabic?
lessons.homework: Write five times of your day in Arabic, for example prayer times and lesson times.
lessons.send: SEND: clocks with Arabic numerals printed. EAL: ordinal numbers table with transliteration. Stretch: add 'twenty past' and 'twenty-five to' using وَثُلُثٌ / إِلَّا ثُلُثًا.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Time and my daily routine
lessons.title: Present tense: you, we and they
objectives: Conjugate a regular verb for I, you (m/f), he, she, we and they
Choose the correct prefix and ending
Use the verbs in short sentences
starter: Say 'I live in London' and 'she reads the book'.
What time is the Dhuhr prayer today? Answer in Arabic.
Give the Arabic for 'she goes to school'.

teach.heading: The verb كَتَبَ
bullets: أَنَا أَكْتُبُ - anā aktubu - I write
هُوَ يَكْتُبُ - huwa yaktubu - he writes
هِيَ تَكْتُبُ - hiya taktubu - she writes
أَنْتَ تَكْتُبُ - anta taktubu - you (m) write
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Revise the three forms from Year 6, then add 'you'. Colour code prefixes: أَ (I), يَ (he), تَ (she/you). Misconception: hiya and anta both use تَ; the context tells us who. Practise by pointing to different pupils on the screen.

teach.heading: You (f), we, they
bullets: أَنْتِ تَكْتُبِينَ - anti taktubīna - you (f) write
نَحْنُ نَكْتُبُ - naḥnu naktubu - we write
هُمْ يَكْتُبُونَ - hum yaktubūna - they (m) write
هُنَّ يَكْتُبْنَ - hunna yaktubna - they (f) write
teach.note: Introduce the extra endings: -īna (you f), نَ prefix (we), -ūna (they m), -na (they f). Note that the present tense يَكْتُبُونَ has no silent alif after the waw (that appears in the past, كَتَبُوا, in Lesson 10). Chorally drill all eight forms in a chain around the class.

teach.heading: Other regular verbs
bullets: يَذْهَبُ - yadhhabu - he goes
يَشْرَبُ - yashrabu - he drinks
يَقْرَأُ - yaqra'u - he reads
يَلْعَبُ - yalʿabu - he plays
teach.note: Give pupils the root pattern: the same prefixes and endings work on all these verbs. Ask them to build 'we go', 'you (f) drink', 'they read' (m). Misconception: forgetting the final -u (damma) on the verb. Remind pupils that the damma is a sign of the present tense.

teach.heading: Short sentences
bullets: نَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ - nadhhabu ilā l-masjid - we go to the mosque
هُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ فِي الْحَدِيقَةِ - they play in the garden
أَنْتِ تَقْرَئِينَ الْقُرْآنَ - you (f) read the Qur'an
هُنَّ يَشْرَبْنَ الْمَاءَ - they (f) drink water
teach.note: Say these sentences with the class and then change the subject. Note the vowel on إِلَى + noun (kasra). The Qur'an should be mentioned with respect; link to reciting the Qur'an each day. Check the correct form of تَقْرَئِينَ for 'you (f) read'.

teach.heading: Mini-conversation
bullets: مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ؟ - mādhā tafʿalu? - what do you do?
أَقْرَأُ وَأَكْتُبُ - aqra'u wa-aktubu - I read and write
مَاذَا تَفْعَلِينَ؟ - to a girl
نَلْعَبُ مَعًا - we play together
teach.note: Pupils interview each other: question to a boy uses -u, to a girl -ina. Encourage them to swap roles so that both forms are practised. Collect two good pairs to perform.

practice: Write 'we go', 'they (m) play', 'you (f) read'.
Choose the right form: هِيَ (يَكْتُبُ / تَكْتُبُ).
Translate: 'You (m) drink water'.
Ask a girl 'What do you do?'.
independent: Complete a table for ذَهَبَ with eight pronouns.
Write six sentences using six different pronouns.
Pair task: ask and answer what you do in the evening.
exit: Write 'they (m) write' and 'we write'.
What is the ending for 'you (f)' in the present tense?
lessons.homework: Write the full present tense of يَشْرَبُ (to drink) for eight pronouns and two sentences.
lessons.send: SEND: verb table with colour-coded prefixes. EAL: pronoun cards with English glosses. Stretch: add the dual forms يَكْتُبَانِ (they two write).

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Time and my daily routine
lessons.title: My daily routine
objectives: Describe a daily routine in the right order
Use sequencing words
Include prayer and school in the routine
starter: Conjugate يَكْتُبُ for 'we' and 'they'.
Say 'It is quarter past seven' in Arabic.
What is the Arabic for 'then'?

teach.heading: Morning routine
bullets: أَسْتَيْقِظُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ - astayqiẓu fī ṣ-ṣabāḥ - I wake in the morning
أُصَلِّي الْفَجْرَ - uṣallī l-fajr - I pray Fajr
أَغْسِلُ وَجْهِي - aghsilu wajhī - I wash my face
أَتَنَاوَلُ الْفُطُورَ - I have breakfast
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. The Prophet (peace be upon him) taught us to say Bismillah before eating (Bukhari and Muslim). Teach each verb with a mime. Note that أَتَنَاوَلُ and أَسْتَيْقِظُ are longer verbs but they use the same أَ prefix and -u ending. Ask pupils to put the actions in order.

teach.heading: School and afternoon
bullets: أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ - adhhabu ilā l-madrasa - I go to school
أَدْرُسُ فِي الْفَصْلِ - adrusu fī l-faṣl - I study in the class
أَعُودُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ - aʿūdu ilā l-bayt - I return home
أَعْمَلُ الْوَاجِبَ - aʿmalu l-wājib - I do homework
teach.note: TGA is an online school, so ask: how do you 'go' to your lesson? Offer أَدْخُلُ الدَّرْسَ (I enter the lesson). Misconception: using أَذْهَبُ for every movement; أَعُودُ means return. Pupils say their afternoon in two sentences.

teach.heading: Evening
bullets: أَنَامُ مُبَكِّرًا - anāmu mubakkiran - I sleep early
أَقْرَأُ الْقُرْآنَ - aqra'u l-qur'ān - I read the Qur'an
أَتَعَشَّى مَعَ عَائِلَتِي - ata'ashshā maʿa ʿā'ilatī - I have dinner with my family
أُصَلِّي الْعِشَاءَ - I pray Isha
teach.note: Link the evening routine with gratitude and family time. Model a sentence with مَعَ (with), which takes kasra on the next noun: مَعَ عَائِلَتِي. Ask a pupil to describe their evening without naming personal details they do not wish to share.

teach.heading: Sequencing words
bullets: أَوَّلًا أَسْتَيْقِظُ - first I wake up
ثُمَّ أُصَلِّي - then I pray
بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَذْهَبُ - after that I go
أَخِيرًا أَنَامُ - finally I sleep
teach.note: Write the four connectives on the board and ask pupils to build a four-sentence routine. Show a model: أَوَّلًا أَسْتَيْقِظُ، ثُمَّ أُصَلِّي الْفَجْرَ، بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَتَنَاوَلُ الْفُطُورَ، أَخِيرًا أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ. Remind about commas ( ، ) and the Arabic punctuation.

teach.heading: Add times
bullets: فِي السَّاعَةِ السَّابِعَةِ - at seven o'clock
أَسْتَيْقِظُ فِي السَّاعَةِ الْخَامِسَةِ - I wake at five
أَنَامُ فِي السَّاعَةِ التَّاسِعَةِ - I sleep at nine
teach.note: Combine the time work from the last lesson with routine verbs. Pupils write three sentences with a time. Focus on the kasra after فِي: السَّاعَةِ, السَّابِعَةِ.

practice: Put the sentences in order: أَنَامُ / أَسْتَيْقِظُ / أُصَلِّي الْفَجْرَ / أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ.
Say what you do at 7:00 and 9:00.
Translate: 'First I wake up, then I have breakfast'.
independent: Write a routine of eight sentences using four sequencing words.
Add at least three times to your routine.
Present your routine in pairs; your partner draws the clock times.
exit: Write 'after that I go to school' in Arabic.
Write one sentence about your evening.
lessons.homework: Write your weekend routine in Arabic with at least six verbs.
lessons.send: SEND: picture sequence cards with verbs. EAL: bilingual verb list with audio. Stretch: write the routine of a family member using هُوَ / هِيَ.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Time and my daily routine
lessons.title: Days of the week and my timetable
objectives: Name the seven days of the week
Say what lesson you have on each day
Read and write a short timetable
starter: Put the routine in order using أَوَّلًا, ثُمَّ, أَخِيرًا.
Say the time: 4:45 in Arabic.
What do you do in the evening? Say two things.

teach.heading: The days
bullets: الْأَحَدُ - al-aḥad - Sunday
الِاثْنَيْنِ - al-ithnayn - Monday
الثُّلَاثَاءُ - ath-thulāthā' - Tuesday
الْأَرْبِعَاءُ - al-arbiʿā' - Wednesday
الْخَمِيسُ - al-khamīs - Thursday
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Link the names to numbers: aḥad (one), ithnayn (two), thalātha (three), arbaʿa (four), khamsa (five). This helps with memory. Pupils say the days in order, then say the day before and after.

teach.heading: Friday and Saturday
bullets: الْجُمُعَةُ - al-jumuʿa - Friday
السَّبْتُ - as-sabt - Saturday
يَوْمُ الْجُمُعَةِ - yawmu l-jumuʿa - the day of Friday
أُصَلِّي الْجُمُعَةَ - I pray Jumuʿa
teach.note: Qur'an 62:9 calls believers to remember Allah and hurry to prayer when the call is made on the day of Jumuʿa. Ask how Friday is special in your family. Note the construct يَوْمُ الْجُمُعَةِ (the day of Friday).

teach.heading: School subjects
bullets: الرِّيَاضِيَّاتُ - ar-riyāḍiyyāt - maths
الْعُلُومُ - al-ʿulūm - science
اللُّغَةُ الْإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةُ - English language
التَّارِيخُ - at-tārīkh - history
الْجُغْرَافِيَا - al-jughrāfiyā - geography
teach.note: Show pictures. Ask which subject pupils have today. Note that الرِّيَاضِيَّاتُ and الْعُلُومُ are plurals but we treat them as singular concepts. Pupils say their favourite subject: أُحِبُّ الْعُلُومَ.

teach.heading: My timetable
bullets: يَوْمَ الِاثْنَيْنِ عِنْدِي رِيَاضِيَّاتٌ - on Monday I have maths
يَوْمَ الثُّلَاثَاءِ عِنْدِي عُلُومٌ - on Tuesday I have science
الدَّرْسُ الْأَوَّلُ فِي السَّاعَةِ التَّاسِعَةِ - first lesson at nine
teach.note: Teach عِنْدِي (I have) in the context of the timetable. Note that day names after يَوْمَ take kasra at the end of the second noun: يَوْمَ الِاثْنَيْنِ. Pupils build their own timetable sentences.

teach.heading: Asking about the timetable
bullets: مَاذَا عِنْدَكَ يَوْمَ الْخَمِيسِ؟ - what do you have on Thursday?
عِنْدِي تَارِيخٌ - I have history
مَتَى دَرْسُ الْعُلُومِ؟ - when is science?
teach.note: Make a question-and-answer chain. Use عِنْدَكَ for a boy and عِنْدَكِ for a girl. Collect two examples to perform. Remind pupils to ask politely and answer with الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ where appropriate.

practice: Say the day after Tuesday and the day before Friday.
Say 'On Wednesday I have history'.
Ask a classmate what they have on Thursday.
Translate: 'Science is at ten o'clock'.
independent: Write a weekly timetable for five days in Arabic with times.
Write five sentences about your timetable.
Role-play a conversation about your week.
exit: Write the seven days in Arabic.
How do you say 'I have maths on Monday'?
lessons.homework: Write a paragraph about your week: what you do on each school day and on Friday.
lessons.send: SEND: day cards with number links. EAL: bilingual timetable. Stretch: add the words before/after (قَبْلَ / بَعْدَ) in sentences.

lessons.title: Past tense: I, he and she
objectives: Recognise the past tense of a regular verb
Form the past tense for I, he and she
Say what you did yesterday using simple verbs
starter: Put these in order: أَخِيرًا أَنَامُ / أَوَّلًا أَسْتَيْقِظُ.
Say 'on Tuesday I have science'.
Write 'they (m) write' in Arabic.

teach.heading: The past tense
bullets: كَتَبَ - kataba - he wrote
ذَهَبَ - dhahaba - he went
أَكَلَ - akala - he ate
شَرِبَ - shariba - he drank
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Explain that the dictionary form of an Arabic verb is the 'he' form of the past tense. Chorally say the four verbs. Ask pupils to give the present form of each (yaktubu, yadhhabu, ya'kulu, yashrabu). Show that the past verb often has three fatḥas.

teach.heading: She and I
bullets: كَتَبَتْ - katabat - she wrote
ذَهَبَتْ - dhahabat - she went
كَتَبْتُ - katabtu - I wrote
ذَهَبْتُ - dhahabtu - I went
teach.note: Add -at (sukun on the ت) for she and -tu (damma) for I. Show that the ت has a different vowel: كَتَبَتْ (sukun, she) vs كَتَبْتُ (damma, I). Misconception: pupils confuse the two and say 'she' for 'I'. Say each form and ask pupils to hold up 1 finger for I, 2 for she, 3 for he.

teach.heading: Using the past
bullets: أَكَلْتُ الْفُطُورَ - akaltu l-futūr - I ate breakfast
ذَهَبَتْ أُمِّي إِلَى السُّوقِ - mum went to the market
شَرِبَ أَخِي الْمَاءَ - my brother drank water
قَرَأْتُ الْقُرْآنَ - qara'tu l-qur'ān - I read the Qur'an
teach.note: Note the direct objects take fatha (الْفُطُورَ, الْمَاءَ, الْقُرْآنَ) · the object ending of a past sentence. Show how the verb comes before the subject in Arabic (ذَهَبَتْ أُمِّي). Ask pupils to say the English meaning of each and then replace the subject.

teach.heading: Time words for the past
bullets: أَمْسِ - amsi - yesterday
أَمْسِ صَبَاحًا - yesterday morning
الْأُسْبُوعَ الْمَاضِيَ - last week
يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ - on Friday
teach.note: Give time expressions and ask pupils to attach them to the sentences. Note الْأُسْبُوعَ الْمَاضِيَ takes fatha endings as a time phrase. Do not push the explanation: just chunk it. Pupils say two sentences with أَمْسِ.

teach.heading: Gratitude for the day
bullets: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ - praise be to Allah
أَشْكُرُ اللَّهَ - ashkuru llāh - I thank Allah
Look back with gratitude
teach.note: Link the past tense to reflecting on the day with shukr (gratitude). Pupils say one thing they are grateful for from yesterday using the past tense, for example: أَكَلْتُ مَعَ عَائِلَتِي أَمْسِ. Keep it light and positive.

practice: Give the 'she' form of: كَتَبَ, ذَهَبَ, أَكَلَ.
Give the 'I' form of: شَرِبَ, قَرَأَ, لَعِبَ.
Translate: 'My brother ate breakfast yesterday'.
Correct the mistake: ذَهَبَتْ أَنَا إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ.
independent: Write ten sentences in the past using he, she and I.
Write about yesterday in six sentences with أَمْسِ.
Pair work: ask what your partner did yesterday and write down the answers.
exit: Write 'she went' and 'I went' in Arabic.
What is the difference between كَتَبَتْ and كَتَبْتُ?
lessons.homework: Write six sentences about what you did yesterday using the past tense with 'I'.
lessons.send: SEND: verb strips with colour-coded endings. EAL: past-tense verb chart with English. Stretch: notice the hollow verbs قَالَ and نَامَ, whose long vowel shortens in 'I' forms: قُلْتُ (qultu), نِمْتُ (nimtu).

lessons.title: Past tense: you, we and they
objectives: Form the past tense for you (m/f), we and they
Recognise the silent alif in كَتَبُوا
Ask and answer questions about the past
starter: Write the past tense of 'I', 'he' and 'she' for كَتَبَ.
Say 'yesterday I went to the mosque'.
What is the difference between كَتَبَتْ and كَتَبْتُ?

teach.heading: Past endings: you
bullets: كَتَبْتَ - katabta - you (m) wrote
كَتَبْتِ - katabti - you (f) wrote
ذَهَبْتَ - dhahabta - you (m) went
ذَهَبْتِ - dhahabti - you (f) went
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Only the final vowel changes: fatḥa for a boy, kasra for a girl. Pupils show a thumb up for fatḥa and thumb down for kasra. Remind them of how -ka and -ki distinguished the listener in Year 7. Practise with a chain of short questions.

teach.heading: We and they
bullets: كَتَبْنَا - katabnā - we wrote
ذَهَبْنَا - dhahabnā - we went
كَتَبُوا - katabū - they (m) wrote
ذَهَبُوا - dhahabū - they (m) went
teach.note: For 'we' add -nā. For 'they' (m) add -ū and write a silent alif (ا) that is not pronounced: كَتَبُوا. Misconception: pronouncing the alif. For 'they' (f) the ending is -na: كَتَبْنَ. Say each verb and ask pupils to add a subject.

teach.heading: Asking about the past
bullets: مَاذَا فَعَلْتَ أَمْسِ؟ - mādhā faʿalta amsi? - what did you do yesterday?
مَاذَا فَعَلْتِ؟ - to a girl
ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ - I went to the mosque
هَلْ ذَهَبْتَ؟ - hal dhahabta? - did you go?
teach.note: Model a question and answer pair, noting the -ta/-ti change in the question and -tu in the answer. Pupils do a pass-the-question game: ask a classmate and write the answer. Remind them to use the right vowel for boys and girls.

teach.heading: Mixed practice
bullets: نَحْنُ ذَهَبْنَا إِلَى السُّوقِ - we went to the market
هُمْ لَعِبُوا كُرَةَ الْقَدَمِ - they played football
أَنْتِ قَرَأْتِ الْكِتَابَ - you (f) read the book
teach.note: Show the three subjects and have pupils change the pronoun. The pronoun is optional in Arabic since the ending shows the subject: ذَهَبْنَا إِلَى السُّوقِ is enough. Ask pupils why we can drop the pronoun.

teach.heading: Negatives in the past
bullets: لَمْ أَذْهَبْ - lam adhhab - I did not go
لَمْ يَكْتُبْ - lam yaktub - he did not write
لَمْ نَأْكُلْ - lam na'kul - we did not eat
teach.note: Introduce لَمْ + present verb with a sukun at the end as a chunk meaning 'did not'. Do not explain the grammar fully: just tell pupils that لَمْ changes the verb ending to sukun and the meaning to the past. Pupils practise: 'I did not eat' and 'she did not go'.

practice: Give the 'you (m)', 'you (f)' and 'we' forms of أَكَلَ.
Translate: 'They (m) went to the mosque'.
Ask a girl what she did yesterday.
Make this negative: ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى السُّوقِ.
independent: Write a table of the past tense of ذَهَبَ for all eight persons.
Write eight sentences about last weekend with different subjects.
Interview a partner: five questions with فَعَلْتَ/فَعَلْتِ and write the answers.
exit: Write 'we ate' and 'they (m) wrote' in Arabic.
How do you say 'I did not go'?
lessons.homework: Write an interview with a family member about what they did yesterday, with five questions and answers in Arabic.
lessons.send: SEND: past endings colour-coded cards. EAL: bilingual pronoun and ending chart. Stretch: include the dual forms كَتَبَا and كَتَبَتَا.

lessons.title: Talking about last weekend
objectives: Describe past events in a short text
Combine past verbs with time words and connectives
Ask follow-up questions
starter: Say 'you (m) went' and 'you (f) went'.
Say 'we did not eat' in Arabic.
Name three time words for the past.

teach.heading: Weekend verbs
bullets: زُرْتُ جَدِّي - zurtu jaddī - I visited my grandfather
لَعِبْنَا كُرَةَ الْقَدَمِ - laʿibnā kurata l-qadam - we played football
ذَهَبْنَا إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ - we went to the mosque
طَبَخَتْ أُمِّي - ṭabakhat ummī - my mother cooked
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Introduce new verbs زَارَ (visit), لَعِبَ (play), طَبَخَ (cook). Notice that زَارَ has a long vowel: زُرْتُ shortens it when we add -tu. Do not teach the full rule yet; present زُرْتُ as a chunk. Ask pupils to give one thing they did last weekend.

teach.heading: Giving details
bullets: مَعَ مَنْ؟ - maʿa man? - with whom?
مَعَ أَصْدِقَائِي - maʿa aṣdiqā'ī - with my friends
فِي الْحَدِيقَةِ - in the garden
كَانَ الْيَوْمُ مُمْتِعًا جِدًّا - the day was very enjoyable
teach.note: Show how to add where, who with and an opinion. كَانَ + noun + predicate in accusative (مُمْتِعًا) · give this as a model sentence: pupils copy the pattern. Note jiddan means 'very' and always follows the adjective.

teach.heading: Connecting ideas
bullets: ثُمَّ - thumma - then
وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ - and after that
وَلَكِنْ - walākin - but
لِأَنَّ - because
teach.note: Use the connectives to build a short story: زُرْتُ جَدِّي، ثُمَّ ذَهَبْنَا إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ، وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ لَعِبْنَا فِي الْحَدِيقَةِ. Ask pupils to find the verbs and sort them by person. Check use of the commas.

teach.heading: A model text
bullets: أَمْسِ زُرْتُ جَدِّي وَجَدَّتِي - yesterday I visited
ثُمَّ أَكَلْنَا مَعًا - then we ate together
بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ صَلَّيْنَا الْعَصْرَ - after that we prayed Asr
كَانَ يَوْمًا جَمِيلًا - it was a beautiful day
teach.note: Read the model aloud. Pupils underline all past tense verbs and the connectives. Ask which verbs are 'I' and which are 'we'. Ask what the family did after the meal. Explain that صَلَّيْنَا uses the doubled lam; show the shadda.

teach.heading: Check your writing
bullets: Verb endings match the subject
Time words included
Add one opinion with جِدًّا
teach.note: Introduce the writing checklist and ask pupils to use it. Remind them of the vowel marks and the punctuation. Praise accurate use of plural -ū and -nā. Give them five minutes to start the writing task.

practice: Say what you did last weekend in three sentences.
Ask a classmate: 'Did you go to the park?'
Turn into the past: أَزُورُ جَدِّي / أَلْعَبُ مَعَ أَصْدِقَائِي.
independent: Write a 60-word text about last weekend using at least six past tense verbs.
Add two connectives and one opinion.
Swap and give your partner two questions about their text.
exit: Write 'I visited my grandmother' in Arabic.
Give two connectives you used today.
lessons.homework: Finish your weekend text neatly with full vowels and learn to read it aloud.
lessons.send: SEND: sentence builder with verb, who and where. EAL: model text with audio. Stretch: write the text from the viewpoint of a sibling using هُوَ / هِيَ.

lessons.title: Review and assessment: reading and writing
objectives: Read a short Arabic passage and answer questions in English
Write a paragraph using the Phase 1 grammar
Reflect on strengths and next steps
starter: Say 'I went to my grandfather's house yesterday'.
Say the time: 6:30 and 8:45.
Make a phrase with a noun and an adjective: 'a spacious house'.

teach.heading: Reading strategy
bullets: Read the questions first
Underline words you know
Guess new words from context
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Explain how to approach a reading text: look at the title, read the questions, then scan for the answer. Show how to use known words (verbs, time words). Stress that you do not need every word to answer.

teach.heading: Model passage
bullets: أَسْتَيْقِظُ فِي السَّاعَةِ الْخَامِسَةِ وَالنِّصْفِ - I wake at 5:30
أُصَلِّي الْفَجْرَ ثُمَّ أَتَنَاوَلُ الْفُطُورَ - I pray Fajr, then have breakfast
أَمْسِ ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ مَعَ أَبِي - yesterday I went with my father
teach.note: Read the passage aloud and ask for the gist. Ask: when does the writer wake up? What do they do after Fajr? Where did they go yesterday and with whom? Model how to answer in English with a full sentence.

teach.heading: Writing plan
bullets: Plan: home, routine, yesterday
Use: هَذَا / هَذِهِ, adjectives, prepositions
Use: present and past tense
teach.note: Pupils plan a paragraph using the Phase 1 topics: home, routine, the past. Show how to tick off the features. Remind them to include sequencing words and times. Allow bilingual dictionaries only if the school permits.

teach.heading: Common mistakes
bullets: ة to ت before -ī
Adjective not matching the noun
Mixing -tu and -at in the past
teach.note: Share three typical mistakes collected during Phase 1 and ask pupils to correct them. Praise the effort. Link to ihsan: checking our work is part of doing things well. Use an error-correction game with pupils voting for the correct version.

teach.heading: Targets
bullets: What I can do now
What I need to practise
My next target
teach.note: Ask pupils to write a target for next half term. Examples: remember the 'she' and 'I' endings, use more connectives. Collect the targets for the teacher record and thank pupils for their effort.

practice: Read the passage and answer: When does the writer wake up?
Find three past tense verbs in the passage.
Translate the second sentence into English.
independent: Re-read the model passage and answer in English: When does the writer wake up? Which prayer comes first? What does the writer eat? Where did they go yesterday? With whom?
Write a paragraph of 80 words on 'My home and my day'.
Self-assess using the checklist and write one target.
exit: Write one sentence about your home and one about yesterday.
State one target for the next unit.
lessons.homework: Practise reading your paragraph aloud and learn ten words from the Phase 1 lists.
lessons.send: SEND: reading passage with highlighted glossary. EAL: bilingual glossary for the passage. Stretch: write a second paragraph comparing your day with your grandparent's day.
